hypothesis: A normal fault is a step, not only a ridge: basement depth, isostatic gravity and detrended elevation change level across the fault and stay changed. Strike-elongated flank-patch contrasts at +-4 px and +-9 px across the visible-catalogue strike on six bands (signed step, |step|, noise-normalised step, centre-line deviation, cross-scale sharpness) measure that throw where pointwise derivatives at sigma<=3 px see only a weak diffuse gradient, in particular for covered intrabasin strands absent from the surface catalogue. An HGB learner on raw19 + 54 STEP features (replacing all pointwise iso/steered derivatives) therefore ranks withheld fault pixels higher per emitted dot than the H78-A pointwise learner.
non_fault_mimic: Lithologic/intrusive contacts and basin-margin facies changes are also cross-strike level changes without a fault.
